h1: Missoniya Hotel — Quiet Japanese Boutique in Bangkok's Kaset District, Spotless Rooms from ฿620
intro: If you walk along Ngamwongwan Road and notice an understated sign with a calm, minimalist aesthetic inside — that is Missoniya Hotel. A 42-room boutique hotel that has been quietly delivering Japanese-style simplicity since 2010, at 44/45 Ngamwongwan Road, Lat Yao, Chatuchak. Bus routes 134 and 191 stop directly outside, making it easy to reach without a car. The MRT Purple Line and BTS Green Line (Kasetsart University station) are reachable by connecting transport. Rates start from approximately ฿620–800/night and the hotel holds a score of 8.7/10 from 410 Agoda reviews — with cleanliness rated an outstanding 9.6/10.

body.html: The big picture: how does a 42-room hotel earn 400-plus reviews scoring 8.7? Missoniya Hotel does not try to do more than its competitors — it simply does a handful of things very well. Cleanliness, calm, and a distinctly Japanese-minimalist atmosphere are the three things guests mention most. Clean lines, muted tones, no decorative clutter — multiple reviewers write that they feel noticeably more relaxed here than at other hotels in the same price bracket. The people who regularly stay here, based on real review data, include business travellers with appointments in the Ngamwongwan–Kaset corridor, parents visiting students at Kasetsart University Bangkhen, transient travellers using Bangkok's northern transit links, and cost-conscious visitors who prefer a quieter city-edge location.

Location and getting around: what does Ngamwongwan actually connect to? The hotel sits at 44/45 Ngamwongwan Road, right on the bus corridor. Routes 134 and 191 stop directly in front — Route 134 runs toward Don Mueang Airport and the old city; Route 191 loops through outer Bangkok. The MRT Purple Line (nearest station is approximately 6 km away; a short Grab ride or connecting bus from the hotel) links to the Blue Line at Tao Poon, from where Chatuchak, Silom, and Asoke are within 30 minutes. The BTS Green Line at Kasetsart University station is about 3 km away — reachable by bus 134 from outside the hotel. Nearby on foot or by motorbike taxi: Pantip Plaza Ngamwongwan (~500 m), MOCA Bangkok Museum of Contemporary Art (~1.3 km). The Mall Ngamwongwan is about 3 km by vehicle. To be direct: this location is ideal for people with business in this district, less ideal as a base for daily sightseeing scattered across Bangkok.
"Room was very clean, smelled great in the lobby, front desk staff always smiling. Convenient — 7-Eleven right next to the hotel. Good value for the price."

Rooms and what you get — Five room categories across 42 units: Standard Double Bed Non-Smoking (two single beds, no smoking), Superior King Room (double bed), King Room with Deluxe Patio View (King bed, private balcony), Deluxe Corner King Room (King bed, corner position, wider views, private balcony). All rooms include air conditioning, TV with YouTube/Netflix, mini-fridge, bottled water, free Wi-Fi, and a clean private bathroom. The Deluxe rooms with a balcony consistently receive the warmest reviews — guests describe having morning coffee on the private terrace as one of the stay's highlights. One thing to know: rooms facing the main road can have noticeable traffic noise, especially from street-facing units. Requesting a quieter side is worth doing at check-in.

Facilities — Small hotel, but covers the essentials: free Wi-Fi throughout, on-site parking (very limited — see below), 24-hour front desk, elevator, security staff, and a taxi-calling service available around the clock through reception. A convenience store is steps away. There is no swimming pool, no fitness centre, and breakfast is not included — these are the three most common dealbreakers for guests who later leave negative feedback after not checking in advance. Plenty of affordable breakfast spots open early within a few minutes' walk in this student neighbourhood.

What real guests say — Based on Agoda (410 reviews, score 8.9/10; sub-scores: cleanliness 9.6, service 8.8, location 8.6, amenities 7.8) and Trip.com (17 reviews, score 8.7/10). What guests praise: exceptional cleanliness for the price point, friendly and helpful front desk staff, pleasant lobby scent and peaceful ambiance, comfortable beds with consistent air conditioning, TV streaming, convenience of the 7-Eleven next door, and affordable room rates. What guests flag: parking is the most-mentioned issue by far — only 2–3 cars can park on site, which regularly disappoints self-driving guests. Street-facing rooms have traffic noise. Wi-Fi can be slow in some areas. A few reviewers noted the night-shift staff were less attentive than the day team. Hair dryers are not available in all room categories (Deluxe rooms have them; standard rooms may not).
"Parking is very limited — only 2–3 spaces. Call ahead if you're driving. But the room itself was great, very clean and the staff were kind. If I'm not driving, this is a perfect choice."

Pricing and value — Standard Double from approximately ฿620–750/night in standard periods. Superior King around ฿700–850. Deluxe King with Patio around ฿800–900. Deluxe Corner King around ฿900–1,000. Rates can rise during public holidays or Kasetsart University events. Comparing Agoda and Trip.com before booking generally finds the best rate. For the Kaset–Ngamwongwan area, where boutique hotels of this quality are sparse, Missoniya offers genuine value for guests who prioritise cleanliness and a calm atmosphere over pool or breakfast inclusions.

Straight verdict — Missoniya Hotel is the best choice in the Kaset–Ngamwongwan area for travellers who want spotless rooms, a distinctive Japanese aesthetic, and good value without paying for four-star facilities. The intentional design language — minimal, composed, restful — sets it apart from generic business hotels in this corridor. The caveats are real: parking is critically limited, there is no pool or gym, and the location suits those with specific business in this area far better than those who want a sightseeing base. Know these going in, and Missoniya will very likely exceed your expectations.

honestSummary: Missoniya Hotel is the most distinctive boutique option in the Kaset–Ngamwongwan area for guests who prioritise cleanliness, calm, and Japanese-minimalist style at under ฿1,000/night. The parking situation is genuinely problematic for drivers, and the lack of pool/gym/breakfast is not negotiable — know these before booking.
honestChecks: If you are driving and need parking — on-site parking holds only 2–3 cars and fills quickly. Call 02-591-9050 in advance to reserve a space or ask about nearby street parking, otherwise plan on alternative transport.

If you need a pool, fitness centre, or breakfast included — Missoniya has none of these. For those amenities at a similar price point in this area, consider Livotel Hotel @ Kaset Nawamin (159 rooms, gym) or The Maruay Garden Hotel (pool, restaurant).

If your plan is to sightsee across Bangkok every day — Ngamwongwan is in Bangkok's northern suburbs. Reaching Silom or Sukhumvit takes 45–60 minutes by connecting transit. This hotel makes most sense for people whose main activities are in the Kaset–Ngamwongwan corridor.

faq.q: Where exactly is Missoniya Hotel located in Bangkok?
faq.a: Missoniya Hotel is at 44/45 Ngamwongwan Road, Lat Yao, Chatuchak, Bangkok 10900. Nearby landmarks include Pantip Plaza Ngamwongwan (~500 m walk), MOCA Bangkok Museum of Contemporary Art (~1.3 km), The Mall Ngamwongwan (~3 km by car), and Kasetsart University Bangkhen (~3.5 km by car). Bus routes 134 and 191 stop directly outside the hotel.

faq.q: Can I reach Missoniya Hotel by BTS or MRT?
faq.a: Yes, with a connecting leg. The BTS Green Line (Kasetsart University station) is about 3 km away — take bus route 134 from outside the hotel to Kaset intersection. The MRT Purple Line is approximately 6 km away, reachable by Grab or connecting bus. For straightforward door-to-door travel, Grab or a taxi from the station is easiest.

faq.q: What is the starting price at Missoniya Hotel?
faq.a: Rates start from approximately ฿620/night for a Standard Double. Superior King rooms are around ฿700. The Deluxe King with a private balcony runs about ฿800. The Deluxe Corner King is around ฿900. Prices can increase during Thai public holidays or Kasetsart University events — compare Agoda and Trip.com before booking.

faq.q: Is there parking at Missoniya Hotel?
faq.a: There is on-site parking, but it is very limited — only 2–3 spaces. If you are driving, call the hotel in advance at 02-591-9050 to check availability, otherwise spaces may already be full on arrival.

Breakfast is not included in any rate. However, the Ngamwongwan area has many affordable breakfast spots — congee, noodle soup, and local coffee shops open from 6 am at ฿40–70 per meal, within a short walk of the hotel.

faq.q: Who is Missoniya Hotel best suited for?
faq.a: It suits business travellers with appointments in the Ngamwongwan–Kaset area, parents visiting Kasetsart University students, and travellers who want a calm, clean boutique stay at a budget price. It is less suited for guests who need a pool or gym, guests arriving by car (very limited parking), or those who plan to sightsee across central Bangkok daily.
